newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-JB Were bearish on copper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-JB Were bearish on copper.

text.p: Brokerage firm J.B. Were and Son Ltd has forecast a fall in copper prices in the second half of calendar 1997, but is bullish for other metal prices.

J.B. Were said in its March quarter review of commodity markets that the rally in base metal prices seen in early 1997 should continue, driven by a moderately positive outlook for the world economy and the need for restocking.
The report tipped nickel and zinc as the most attractive commodities, but said copper was a different story.
"While the demand outlook for copper looks healthy enough, we remain bearish on its medium and longer term prospects," it said.

"At present the market is very tight, and we do not expect to see a clear move to surplus until late in the first half of the year. But there is very good reason to believe that the second half will see a swing to substantial oversupply, and that prices will ease considerably at that time."
It forecast LME copper to fall to a low of 79 U.S. cents per pound by the second half of 1998. Spot copper is trading at around US$1.21 per pound.
